Finding in PR https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/pull/1750, supporting https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1734.

The new read-only MediaDive archive qualification verifier fails on supported Python 3.10 before it can inspect endpoint evidence. `archive_metadata()` wraps a member returned by `tarfile.open(..., mode="r|")` in `io.TextIOWrapper`. On Python 3.10.11, wrapper initialization calls `ExFileObject.seekable()`, which delegates to the stream-mode `_Stream`; that object has no `seekable` attribute.

The coordinated offline run stopped after five failures in 2.62 seconds. Both real archive success controls and the first three restamped-metadata controls fail at `scripts/adhoc/kgm_mediadive_artifact_admission_20261105.py:235` with `AttributeError: '_Stream' object has no attribute 'seekable'`. The saved log is `data/rebuild-evidence/20261105/mediadive-resolution-1734/remaining-consumer-and-artifact-focused-r1.log` (SHA256 `95dab4657ef19189afda8b1117acacd0d942f6b137d247ee77aa5dde6c0a5ffb`).

Replace the seeking text wrapper with `codecs.iterdecode(stream, "utf-8")`. The binary member iterator supplies physical TSV lines; incremental decoding preserves UTF-8, and the existing `csv.DictReader(..., quoting=csv.QUOTE_NONE)` continues to validate the finite endpoint audit. Graph TSVs remain streamed, archive extraction remains read-only, and manifest/body/admission comparisons are unchanged.

Acceptance: rerun the existing `tests/test_mediadive_artifact_admission_20261105.py` controls through the coordinated test window. The existing actual-archive positive cases must pass; restamped metadata, malformed endpoint inventories and source-drift cases must still reject. No tests were added or weakened and no production source, graph, policy, or historical receipt changed. The fix is prepared; its pytest rerun is pending root coordination.
title: MediaDive artifact verifier: stream-mode tar reader fails on Python 3.10

MediaDive ingredient 1944 has a blank name and is reused for three different preparations. A global mapping from `mediadive.ingredient:1944` to yeast extract would also misidentify Trypticase peptone and MES rows. This is a source-identity defect; this review does not establish that the current KG emits a wrong chemical endpoint.

The worker01 canary is bound to MIM base `e000d66dd26ab053e9b17ce7bf8d3c873c3dde99` and dependency [MIM #1158](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/pull/1158). Its exact source case is `KG_CASE:e431bbfe8e78c226a9a06d038b7944f91e4580b44fe5b9e2c83d0e236c6d23cf`. Frozen `compounds.json` SHA256 is `5401db0bc697249c9b2b0ad0b950fd3c2b7629f0cdd10c7feaf1e40b0a3a4729`; object key `1944` retains `compound: ""`, attribute `w/v) Yeast extract (BD-Difco, 10%`, 5 ml, recipe order 12.

Complete admitted source context and live primary recipes distinguish:

| Recipe / solution / recipe_order | Native attribute | Original recipe meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| J935 / 4947 / 12 | `w/v) Yeast extract (BD-Difco, 10%` | 5 ml of a 10% w/v BD-Difco yeast-extract solution |
| J935 / 4947 / 13 | `w/v) Trypticase peptone (BD-BBL, 10%` | 20 ml of a 10% w/v BD-BBL Trypticase-peptone solution |
| J1053 / 5115 / 13 | `w/v) MES (pH 6.0, 20%` | 10 ml of a 20% w/v MES solution at pH 6.0 |

Primary sources: [MediaDive ingredient](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/ingredients/1944), [ingredient JSON](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/download/ingredient/1944/json), [J935 JSON](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/rest/medium/J935), [J1053 JSON](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/rest/medium/J1053), [original JCM 935](https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=935), and [original JCM 1053](https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1053). Retrieved 2026-11-08 UTC. The two live recipe responses match the retained admitted response bodies byte for byte. The three solution rows repeat the same three recipe rows; they are not six independent occurrences. The queue's `occurrences: 1` is explicitly a helper constant.

The ingredient JSON also gives `chebi_id: 1`. [EBI OLS ChEBI:1](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms?obo_id=CHEBI:1) marks it obsolete with replacement [CHEBI:18357](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms?obo_id=CHEBI:18357), `(R)-noradrenaline`. Neither this source cross-reference nor a broad yeast-extract ontology term resolves the incompatible preparations.

Keep a source-scoped hold. No native MIM owner is identified, no alias/ontology/SSSOM edit is proposed, and no existing release hold is removed. Source correction belongs in MediaDive's ingredient/recipe representation or a separately reviewed, source-bound downstream correction that retains original records and uses recipe/solution/list-position identity. A bare component mapping must not replace a stock.

Acceptance for future resolution:

- Obtain corrected MediaDive ingredient identities for each preparation, or an explicit reviewed occurrence-scoped correction with the original source ID and raw fields retained.
- Preserve each recipe's stock concentration, supplier where stated, pH, amount, unit, order, and provenance; do not infer a catalog SKU or an exact supplied chemical form absent from the recipe.
- Reassess any intended MIM stock/ingredient owners independently and pass the normal owner-content and publication gates before releasing mappings.
- Recheck all three source contexts and the erroneous source cross-reference; a correction to the yeast row alone cannot resolve the global blank ID.

This is a bounded source finding from the unmatched-source canary. Related [MIM #1157](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/1157) addresses five different IDs; [#718](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/718), [#811](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/811) and [#868](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/868) are broader material/alias queues. They do not themselves resolve this shared blank `compound_id`. KG-Microbe #1009 closes a finite instruction/recipe-pair review, rather than this source-ID collision. This follows the read-only source review associated with #1788. Exact-ID and comment searches in both repositories found no existing 1944 finding; broader searches were bounded and are retained in the evidence. Existing issues remain open/closed as observed; no issue closure is requested.

Its native requests write that cache before the helper can validate all endpoint outcomes and atomically replace the strain JSON. An abrupt interruption can therefore leave fresh cache rows beside the preceding JSON generation, or a new JSON generation before a completed retry receipt.

The current design preserves exact original files/sidecars and standalone before/phase snapshots, never emits association admission before final verification, and refuses changed baselines on a later attempt. A private cache generation is one possible architecture, but it must be reconciled with the requested production-path canary/output identity. This finding does not waive the present canary, coverage or admission gates. Related #1734 and PR #1750.

The #1734 retry review found that the production bulk format and lookup cannot distinguish an unknown association response from a valid empty list.

`kg_microbe/utils/mediadive_bulk_download.py::get_json_from_api` returns `{}` on HTTP/transport failure; `download_medium_strains` omits falsy results. A successful explicit `data: []` is also omitted. `kg_microbe/transform_utils/mediadive/mediadive.py::get_json_object` then returns `[]` for any absent strain key, describing it as an empty response. The five-input bulk contract binds exact JSON bytes but carries no endpoint outcome ledger.

Actual preserved evidence from the M5 run contains 2,712 nonempty successful strain responses and 632 unresolved endpoints, with zero valid empty responses. Every unresolved endpoint previously returned HTTP404 at least once. Official API documentation classifies DataNotFound as an error with ambiguous absence/composition causes. Output omission cannot establish a known empty association list.

The current bounded retry helper will retain distinct fresh nonempty, explicit-empty, documented unknown404, transport and invalid outcomes, and will keep combined acquisition admission false while any unknown/error remains. This protects the present rebuild; it does not repair the generic producer contract.

Acceptance for a production contract repair:
- Carry original endpoint outcome evidence through acquisition, consumed-input binding, producer completion and replay/admission; preserve historical receipts and input bytes.
- Distinguish explicit successful empty responses from unknown/unavailable outcomes and transport/malformed failures. Missing evidence must fail closed, not imply empty.
- Validate current outcomes against exact requested IDs, catalogue coverage, fresh response identities and any reviewed finite scientific dispositions. Never use stale-cache fallback or fabricate an empty array.
- Preserve current recipe/association assertions and require offline controls for unknown-versus-empty, stale/altered ledger, missing/extra IDs, redirects, and fresh-instance admission.
- Do not claim complete association coverage or release readiness from classified unknowns. Any change to the complete-response gate needs its own evidence-backed reviewed contract, not a waiver.

Supporting evidence: `data/rebuild-evidence/20261105/mediadive-retry-1734/baseline-review/` and `official-review/official-semantics.json`. Related work: #1734 and PR #1750. No upstream contact is needed or authorized.

## Problem

The download/transform pipeline discourages incremental experimentation. Developers can't easily work on a single data source without triggering the entire pipeline. Caching behavior is undocumented and inconsistent across sources. New contributors have no way to understand what gets downloaded, where it goes, how to clear it, or how long it takes.

This is an umbrella issue. Each checkbox could become its own issue.

---

## 1. Selective download

- [ ] **Add `tag` fields to all items in `download.yaml`** — the `kghub_downloader` framework already supports a `tags` parameter, but zero items in `download.yaml` use it. Group by data source (e.g., `mediadive`, `bacdive`, `ontology`, `ncbitaxon`, `chebi`, `metatraits`)
- [ ] **Expose `--tags` in the `kg download` CLI** — pass through to `download_from_yaml(tags=...)` so users can run `kg download -t mediadive` instead of downloading all 39 items
- [ ] **Parity with transform** — `kg transform -s mediadive` already works per-source; `kg download` should have equivalent granularity

## 2. Caching and incremental updates

- [ ] **Document the two-layer caching for MediaDive** — there's a `requests_cache` SQLite file (per-URL, 50MB) AND output JSONs in `data/raw/mediadive/` (all-or-nothing, 43MB). The PR description doesn't distinguish cached vs uncached behavior
- [ ] **Fix `.gitignore` mismatch** — `.gitignore` has `mediadive_cache.sqlite` but the bulk downloader creates `mediadive_bulk_cache.sqlite`. The 50MB cache file is not gitignored
- [ ] **Gitignore the output JSONs** — `data/raw/mediadive/*.json` (43MB of generated data) is not gitignored
- [ ] **Audit caching behavior for all data sources** — which sources have HTTP caching? Which check for existing files? Which re-download unconditionally? Document the answers
- [ ] **Support per-item updates for MediaDive output** — currently all 4 output JSONs are full dumps. If MediaDive adds one medium, all 3,333 get re-dumped. Consider incremental JSON merge or per-medium files

## 3. Documentation per data source

Each data source should have a brief doc (README section, table, or per-source markdown) covering:

- [ ] **What it downloads** — URLs, expected file count, approximate size
- [ ] **Where output goes** — paths relative to repo root
- [ ] **How to clear/refresh** — which files and caches to delete
- [ ] **Expected timing** — cold download, cached, and transform. For reference: NCBITaxon is 12GB+ and dominates download time; MediaDive bulk is ~43MB and trivial by comparison
- [ ] **Dependencies** — does the transform need other sources' downloads to be present?

## 4. MediaDive parallel download (PR #527) specific

- [ ] **Assess whether parallelization is worth the complexity** — with `requests_cache` in place, the only time parallel matters is a cold-start first download. The 274-line threading addition (semaphores, thread-safe sessions, retry-after) benefits a ~4 min one-time operation on a 43MB dataset, in a repo where NCBITaxon is 12GB
- [ ] **Add execution instructions to PR** — how to run, where output goes, how to clear destination, how to clear cache
- [ ] **Respect the API operator** — MediaDive is a small academic API at DSMZ. Even at 5 workers, saturating their endpoint with concurrent requests for a one-time bulk download is poor etiquette when sequential + caching achieves the same result on every subsequent run
- [ ] **Consider extracting the good parts without the threading** — User-Agent header, Retry-After handling, parameterized retry logic are all valuable independent of parallelization

## 5. Pipeline-wide ergonomics

- [ ] **`kg download` should report what it will do before doing it** — list items, expected sizes, estimated time. A dry-run mode (`--dry-run`) would help
- [ ] **`kg download` should skip already-present files by default** — some sources may already do this, but the behavior is inconsistent and undocumented
- [ ] **Post-download hooks (like MediaDive bulk) should be opt-in** — currently `_post_download_mediadive_bulk` runs automatically after every `kg download` if `mediadive.json` exists. This surprises developers who just wanted to refresh an ontology file

## Context

- PR https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/pull/527 prompted this investigation
- `download.yaml` has 39 items totaling ~21GB in `data/raw/`
- Transform already supports per-source execution (`-s` flag); download does not
- The `kghub_downloader` library supports tags but they're unused here
title: kg download: add a dry-run/plan mode and a per-source download reference (size, location, refresh, timing)

Follow-up from the review of PR #1657 (#1567).

`hpc/submit_phased_transforms.sh` chains phase N+1 on the whole array job of phase N with `afterok`. So one failed source in a phase cancels every later phase (`--kill-on-invalid-dep=yes`), including sources that do not read it. For example, a failed `prego` in phase 1 cancels `mediadive` in phase 2, although `mediadive` declares only `ontologies` and `bacdive`.

`kg transform` behaves differently: it isolates a failure to its source and skips only the sources that declare the failed one in `TRANSFORM_INPUTS`. The strict behaviour fails safe, since nothing runs on a missing upstream, but it can waste a large part of an HPC run.

Possible improvement: submit each source as its own job, with `afterok` on exactly the job IDs of the upstreams it declares. Alternatively, keep phase arrays and depend on individual array tasks (`afterok:<job>_<task>`). Both need the planner to emit each source's upstreams along with its phase.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Phased HPC transform: a failed source cancels later phases even for sources that do not read it

# Mapping-induced graph comparison is not established by aggregate deltas

Read-only finding for #1788 / dependent PR #1804, candidate `f10fb3909ed32898a54176ca77e509a950d16b84`. This is an acceptance-evidence gap, not an observed wrong graph: the new graph has not been produced or scanned in this review. No code, producer, scientific policy or existing admission has been changed.

## Exact current behavior

- `scripts/adhoc/kgm_rebuild_comparison_20261105.py:27–31` selects only the archive, MediaDive edges and stats. It does not bind old/new source producer reports or mapping-row lineage.
- `distribution` at lines130–156 counts rows and category/predicate/source memberships. It discards each row's endpoints, complete properties and occurrence identity after counting.
- `compare` at lines229–264 and277–308 reports those aggregate deltas and ingredient counts. Its existing disclaimer correctly limits the result to description and does not grant semantic admission.
- `scripts/mediadive_coverage_check.py:91–101` increments one count per non-nested ingredient edge per normalized solution. It does not compare ingredient objects, quantities, native source assertions or full source records.

Consequently an old edge `(solution:1, has_part, chemical:A)` replaced by `(solution:1, has_part, chemical:B)` with identical other counted columns produces unchanged totals and ingredient counts. Replacing one of two occurrences with a duplicate of another can likewise preserve every reported count. Changed `source_record`, `source_assertion_id`, concentration, provenance or node labels can also be invisible. These are structural counterexamples derived from the implementation, not claims about the actual retained or future graphs.

Issue #1788 explicitly requires comparing mapping-induced graph changes against the preserved baseline. Aggregate movement alone cannot explain those changes or separate mapping effects from changes in fresh producer inputs, code, output order or deduplication.

## Existing reusable components and limits

An ignored-inclusive filename/content search covered this worktree's native scripts, kg_microbe, tests, `.claude` and retained evidence, excluding Git internals, virtual environments, copied upstream source/runtime and saved `before` snapshots. It found no complete old/new graph-row comparator in that scope. This is a scoped inventory, not an assertion about every external checkout.

- `.claude/skills/kg-release-diff/kg_release_diff.py:141–214,332–479` provides more distributions/type signatures, but still no complete row multiset comparison. It retains node dictionaries in memory and is not the proposed graph-scale implementation.
- `kg_microbe/edge_snapshot.py:154–213` preserves immutable manifest/member/row coordinates and literal source rows in bounded shards. It is useful design precedent, but exports one snapshot rather than comparing two archives.
- E2 `candidate-conservation-independent-r1.py:176–200` already uses bounded SQLite batches and full payload multiplicities for mapping artifacts. Its native SSSOM-specific conservation rules cannot be applied directly to graph semantics.
- Existing source freshness, recipe/material and archive qualification gates remain authoritative. They verify present correctness; they do not explain old/new mapping-related differences. Their logic and thresholds should remain unchanged.

## Proposed disposition

File/triage this finite comparison requirement before implementation. Retain the existing aggregate report and add a separate read-only, identity-bound row/occurrence comparison with source-context attribution, as specified in `graph-comparison-design-r1.md`. Do not relax gates or infer that every graph difference was caused by MIM. Any unclassified change remains visible for review. No helper has been implemented or run by this task.

## Triage and acceptance

In-scope acceptance-evidence blocker for #1788 and PR #1804. Add a separate read-only comparison helper under this isolated run's retained evidence; keep the committed production candidate, original graph and existing admission gates unchanged. Complete focused offline controls and independent review before graph scanning. This does not authorize broader policy changes or publication.

This supplements the accepted mapping review. It creates descriptive evidence, never source completion, scientific admission or release permission. No graph scan, producer, test or comparison implementation was executed during preparation.

Split out of #1642, which noted it as separate and predating #1639. Confirmed by reading SemSQL 0.4.0 (`semsql/builder/builder.py`, `make()`): it runs `subprocess.run(cmd)` with no `check`, so `semsql make` exits 0 even when `make` fails.

As a result, the `except subprocess.CalledProcessError` branch in `_run_semsql_build` (`kg_microbe/utils/ontology_utils.py`) never fires for a failed `make`. A failed build is still caught, because the old database was moved to `.prev` and the new one fails `_usable_db` or `_build_confirmed`. The old database is then restored, so the outcome is correct. What is lost is the message: the user sees "rejecting" or "restoring" rather than "semsql make failed", and the `make` output is the only clue.

Options:
- run `make -f <semsql>/builder/build.Makefile <target>` directly, which is what `semsql make` does with no Docker;
- or check for a `<db>.tmp` left behind, which the `%.db` recipe creates and moves only on success.

Severity: low (diagnostics only; the build outcome is already judged by validation).

The BacDive transform extracts phenotypes comprehensively — **4,243,914 edges** with METPO predicates. But it discards the one thing needed to attribute a statement to the paper it came from.

## What the transform records

`primary_knowledge_source` holds the **strain record**, not the reference:

```
kgmicrobe.strain:bacdive_1  biolink:subclass_of  NCBITaxon:435  ...  ['infores:bacdive', 'bacdive:1']
kgmicrobe.strain:bacdive_1  METPO:2000517  mediadive.medium:105  ...  ['infores:bacdive', 'bacdive:1']
```

Verified on 50,000 edges: the id in `primary_knowledge_source` equals the subject's strain id in **50,000 of 50,000** cases. It identifies which BacDive record an edge came from, never which citation.

## What BacDive actually provides

BacDive attaches an `@ref` to **every individual data item**, and each strain record's `Reference` section maps those ids to citations via a `doi/url` field. So the raw data supports statement-level paper attribution.

`kg_microbe/transform_utils/bacdive/bacdive.py` (3,419 lines) contains **no handling of the `Reference` section** — the only two `@ref` occurrences are in comments.

## Why this matters

The `@ref` linkage is lost at transform time and cannot be reconstructed from the output, because the edge no longer records which data item it came from. Anyone needing "which paper says this organism grows on this medium" has to **re-parse the raw JSON in parallel**, duplicating extraction logic that already exists here.

That is what we ended up doing in `kg-microbe-projects` (`bacdive_doi_triples/`), and the cost of duplicating is exactly what you'd expect: it covers **9 sections** and produces **313,778** DOI-attributed triples, against the transform's 4.24M edges. Roughly **50% of referenced BacDive statements** are missed (excluding phylogeny and provenance sections) — morphology, halophily, culture pH, spore formation and the API panels are absent entirely.

## Suggested change

Emit the `@ref` id per edge — an extra column, or an additional entry in `primary_knowledge_source` alongside the existing strain id. Optionally resolve it to a DOI from the `Reference` section during the transform.

Either way the downstream join becomes trivial and the parallel extraction can be deleted, taking coverage from ~313k attributed statements to potentially all 4.24M.

## Checked against

- `data/transformed/bacdive/edges.tsv` (4,243,914 edges; 3,859,944 carry `bacdive:<id>`)
- `data/raw/bacdive_strains.json`
- `kg_microbe/transform_utils/bacdive/bacdive.py`
title: BacDive: carry item-level reference publications beyond metabolite utilization

Observed 2026-09-10 during the resume after #1045, on the 64 GB machine.

## What happened

One invocation, in `TRANSFORM_INPUTS` order:

```
kg transform -s ontologies -s gtdb -s lpsn -s bacdive -s mediadive -s metatraits -s metatraits_gtdb -s gold -s prego -s lpsn_api -s microbedecoder
```

By the time `metatraits` started, 2h54m in, the parent process held **9.9 GB RSS**. Nothing is released between sources: every transform runs in the same interpreter and leaves its label maps, mapping loaders and DataFrames reachable or fragmented. `metatraits` then forked its Pool of 6 workers from that parent; each was at ~900 MB and climbing (refcount writes defeat copy-on-write), the machine went to 0.9 GB free / 14 GB swap, and the chunk rate fell from **~420 it/s** (the same step, same code, same input, in the 2026-09-10 rebuild log) to **5.86 it/s** — 70x slower, a ~50 h projection for a 42-minute step.

`bacdive` had already shown the milder form an hour earlier: 3.1 GB RSS and a rate that tracked machine load minute by minute.

## Why it matters now

#685 made the multi-source invocation the recommended way to run a batch: one call, per-source isolation, dependency-aware skipping. That is right for failure semantics but wrong for memory, and the two are now in tension. The scratch driver it replaced (`run_transforms.sh`, one `kg transform -s X` per source) never had this problem because each source got a fresh interpreter.

## Fix shapes, in rough order of value

1. **Run each source in a subprocess** from `transform()`'s loop. Keeps #685's isolation, skipping and summary exactly as they are — the parent only supervises — and every source starts from a fresh interpreter. This is the correct fix.
2. Failing that, explicit `gc.collect()` plus dropping references between sources helps only marginally; fragmentation and C-extension allocations (pandas, sqlite, oaklib) do not come back.
3. Independently, `metatraits` could start its Pool with `spawn` rather than `fork`, so workers do not inherit the parent's heap at all. Slower startup, but it is what CLAUDE.md's "resolve adapters in the parent before creating a Pool" rule already implies is safe.

## Acceptance

Run the full source list in one invocation on the same machine and confirm the `metatraits` chunk rate matches a standalone `kg transform -s metatraits` within noise, and that parent RSS immediately before `metatraits` starts is a fresh-interpreter baseline rather than the sum of everything before it.

Workaround today: run `metatraits` (and any other Pool-forking source) as its own invocation.

Related: #685, #693 (the merge has the same one-process shape), #1045.
title: A multi-source kg transform accumulates memory across sources, so a later transform that forks a Pool inherits a ~10 GB parent and thrashes

## Summary

`kgm-freshness-check` gives **different answers depending on how it is launched**,
with nothing in the output saying so. Under bare `python` it silently loses both
the content fingerprint and every `DATA_INPUTS` declaration, and the resulting
verdicts are *more optimistic* than the truth — which is the exact failure mode
#812 was filed to eliminate.

Found while verifying #879's fix.

## Reproduction

Same script, same working tree, same commit (b2f1ad1c), back to back:

```
$ python      .claude/skills/kgm-freshness-check/kgm_freshness_check.py
$ poetry run python .claude/skills/kgm-freshness-check/kgm_freshness_check.py
```

| source | bare `python` | `poetry run` |
|---|---|---|
| gold | `STALE_VS_CODE` | **`FRESH`** |
| madin_etal | `STALE_VS_CODE` | **`STALE_VS_CODE_AND_DATA`** |
| mediadive | `STALE_VS_CODE` | **`STALE_VS_CODE_AND_DATA`** |
| metatraits | `STALE_VS_CODE` | **`STALE_VS_CODE_AND_DATA`** |
| metatraits_gtdb | `STALE_VS_CODE` | **`STALE_VS_CODE_AND_DATA`** |
| microbedecoder | `STALE_VS_CODE` | **`STALE_VS_CODE_AND_DATA`** |
| ontologies_stubs | `STALE_VS_CODE` | **`STALE_VS_CODE_AND_DATA`** |

Summary line, bare: `STALE_VS_DATA 0`, `STALE_VS_CODE_AND_DATA 0`.
Summary line, poetry: `STALE_VS_CODE_AND_DATA 6`, `FRESH 1`.

**Six sources are stale against their curation data and the bare run does not say
so.** A `mappings/` correction lands, the operator runs the pre-flight, sees only
`STALE_VS_CODE`, and has no signal that the data moved — #812, reintroduced
through the tool built to detect it.

## Cause

Three helpers all swallow the import and degrade to "nothing declared":

- `_fingerprint_verdict` — `except ImportError: return None` → falls back to timestamps
- `_declared_data_inputs` — `except Exception: return ()` → no data staleness possible
- `_declared_transform_inputs` — `except Exception: return ()` → no `STALE_VS_UPSTREAM` possible

The import fails because `kg_microbe/__init__.py` eagerly imports the whole CLI surface:

```
kg_microbe/__init__.py:6      from .download import download
kg_microbe/download.py:8      from kghub_downloader.download_utils import download_from_yaml
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'kghub_downloader'
```

So reading a pure-stdlib helper (`kg_microbe.utils.transform_fingerprint` imports
only `ast`, `hashlib`, `json`, `pathlib`) drags in the full dependency set. This
is the same shape as the CLAUDE.md rule *"imports used only by one CLI command
must remain command-local"*, applied to the package `__init__` rather than to a
command.

The degradation is deliberate — `_declared_data_inputs`'s docstring says it is so
the skill "still runs in an environment without kg_microbe importable". That intent
is fine. Degrading **silently, in the optimistic direction** is the bug.

## Suggested fix

Roughly in order of value:

1. **Say when the signal is unavailable.** If the import fails, print a banner:
   `WARNING: kg_microbe not importable — data-input and fingerprint checks are
   DISABLED; verdicts may be optimistic. Rerun with 'poetry run'.` A degraded run
   must not be visually indistinguishable from a complete one.
2. **Make the degraded status honest.** A source whose `DATA_INPUTS` could not be
   read is not `STALE_VS_CODE`; it is "code-stale, data unknown". Consider an
   `UNKNOWN`/`UNVERIFIED` status rather than reporting the optimistic half.
3. **Make the helper importable on its own.** Either make `kg_microbe/__init__.py`
   lazy (the `LazyTransform` pattern already in `transform.py`), or have the skill
   load `transform_fingerprint.py` by file path via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`,
   bypassing the package `__init__` entirely. It has no intra-package imports
   except `atomic_io`, so this is close to free.
4. **Have the skill re-exec under `poetry run`** when the import fails and a
   `poetry` binary is present.

(1) alone removes the trap. (3) removes the cause.

## Verification note

The `poetry run` column is the correct one. Both runs are on b2f1ad1c with a clean
tree; the only difference is the interpreter's import path.
title: kgm-freshness-check: a run without kg_microbe importable is unlabeled and reports existing fingerprints as absent

`RecipeIdentityGuard.verify()` chose the canonical `QUOTE_NONE` reader whenever `source_finalization.json` existed in the output directory. Rerunning the producer in place (`kg transform -s mediadive` over a finalized directory) writes pandas-quoted TSVs while the old report is still present. The sealed guard then misreads its own fresh output and aborts with the misleading "MediaDive recipe identity: complete native source record changed". Only the fingerprint is invalidated at run start, so the stale report survives.

**Status:** fixed in #1401. At `write()` the guard records the identity (device, inode, size, mtime) of any pre-existing report, and treats a report as certifying the canonical dialect only if it is not that stale one. Publication always atomically replaces the report. Regression: `test_rerun_over_previous_finalization_writes_and_refinalizes` (run, finalize, rerun with a fresh instance, refinalize).

The same "report exists, so the files are canonical" heuristic remains in `_dependency_declarations` (`source_finalization.py`) for other sources reading the ontologies directory.

Found in the adversarial review of #1401.

Related to #286. This is a **historical source/mapping finding; the currently
running rebuild has not yet been checked**. It neither reproduces #286's old
234-ID cohort nor implies all CAS identities should disappear.

## Evidence

The saved September 27 inventory contains nine `infores:mediadive`
`biolink:has_part` assertions to `cas:93348-51-7`, all for raw
`compound_id=1606`, `compound="Potato"`:

- Six have explicit material-form evidence: solutions **3653, 3678, 3679, 3754,
  4879** have `condition=" peeled and cut"`; solution **840** has
  `attribute="fresh, washed, peeled and sliced"`.
- Three are unqualified Potato: solutions **227, 4051, 5502**. They must not
  inherit the other records' annotations or be described as independently
  proved fresh tubers.
- Source assertion IDs are `mediadive.solution:<id>#recipe/1`, except solution
  227 uses `#recipe/2`. Amounts are retained as 200 g except 3678=300 g,
  3679=30 g, and 5502=150 g; `g_l` is supplied, `mmol_l` is not.

The [official EINECS inventory, PDF page 21](https://www.mhsr.sk/uploads/files/Zwx10C5G.pdf)
associates CAS **93348-51-7** / EC **297-194-4** with the entry
`Solanum tuberosum aegrotans, extrakt`, describing extractives and their
physically modified derivatives. [MediaDive ingredient 1606](https://bacmedia.dsmz.de/ingredients/1606)
lists this identifier with fresh-potato wording and warns that identifiers are
largely automatically matched. [Recipe 3653](https://bacmedia.dsmz.de/solutions/3653)
starts with peeled/cut potato, then boils and strains it. Starting material and
prepared extract are not automatically the same identity.

This does not dispute the CAS number's existence. It establishes a scope concern:

# MediaDive Sigma P3556 is assigned a specific phosphatidylcholine species unsupported by its product evidence

Related: #286 historical CAS disposition review. This is a **current source/material-scope defect**, not a claim that the historical CAS `8002-43-5` is globally invalid, and not a request to alter the frozen Potato PR.

## Reproducible current use

The pinned current raw MediaDive files contain compound `2082`, named `L-α-Phosphatidylcholine`, with the explicit attribute `SIGMA P3556`. Solution `629`, recipe array index 0, contains the same full record:

```json
{"recipe_order":1,"compound":"L-α-Phosphatidylcholine","compound_id":2082,"attribute":"SIGMA P3556","amount":5,"unit":"mg","g_l":5,"optional":0}
```

The completed isolated MediaDive replay emits this actual edge, retaining the source record:

```text
mediadive.solution:629 — biolink:has_part → CHEBI:86658
source_assertion_id = mediadive.solution:629#recipe/1
primary_knowledge_source = infores:mediadive
knowledge_level = observation; agent_type = manual_agent
```

It is at `edges.tsv` physical line 110824 in the independently accepted source-only replay. A separate bounded invocation of the **actual** `MediaDiveTransform.standardize_compound_id("2082", "L-α-Phosphatidylcholine")`, using the full pinned unified loader and exact selected raw/legacy evidence, returns `CHEBI:86658` again. No full transform was launched for this diagnostic. All inputs and saved replay outputs remained unchanged.

## Why the identity is too specific

The [official P3556 product sheet](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/deepweb/assets/sigmaaldrich/product/documents/152/475/p3556pis.pdf), page 1, describes an egg-yolk phosphatidylcholine preparation with several fatty-acid constituents: approximately 33% palmitic, 13% stearic, 31% oleic and 15% linoleic acids, plus minor constituents, and an average molecular mass around 768. It does not establish a single acyl-chain composition for the supplied product.

The full pinned raw ChEBI node for `CHEBI:86658` instead specifies one structure, formula `C42H80NO8P`, mass `758.075`, InChIKey `JLPULHDHAOZNQI-JLOPVYAASA-N`, explicit 16:0 and `(9E,12E)` 18:2 acyl-chain synonyms, and an InChI stereolayer `/b16-14+,21-20+`. This evidence is preserved directly from `data/raw/chebi.json`, not inferred solely from its generic display label.

The [current official product page](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sigma/p3556) also displays a single catalog SMILES/InChI alongside the egg-yolk product description. That is acknowledged, not omitted: its InChIKey is `JLPULHDHAOZNQI-ZTIMHPMXSA-N`, with `/b16-14-,21-20-`, so it is not even the same structured identifier as the pinned ChEBI node. More importantly, a catalog structure does not override the manufacturer's explicit variable-composition product sheet. The source does not establish that the material in this recipe is the one specific molecular species represented by `CHEBI:86658`.

The supplier's [polymeric drug-delivery brochure](https://b2b.sigmaaldrich.com/deepweb/assets/sigmaaldrich/marketing/global/documents/709/352/polymeric-drug-delivery-techniques-web.pdf), printed page 17 / PDF index 18, independently illustrates P3556 using variable fatty-acid substituents. Supplier documents were successfully retrieved through the web reader; direct byte-download attempts failed with zero bytes, so no local PDF checksum or immutable upstream PDF pin is claimed.

## Exact current cause

- `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`, record 950 / physical line 987: `MIM:L-alpha-Phosphatidylcholine skos:exactMatch CHEBI:86658`, with lexical matching provenance and the Greek-alpha label in `other`.
- Unified mapping physical line 582877: Greek-alpha name alias selects `CHEBI:86658`. The corresponding MIM identity row is at line 582872; the Latin-alpha canonical-name row is at line 582878.
- `kg_microbe/transform_utils/mediadive/mediadive.py:847` takes the name lookup before legacy/embedded fallback. `get_solution_recipe_occurrences` supplies the name, while the supplier attribute remains only in the retained source record. The current finite identity/hydration guard does not reject this material-to-specific-species assignment.
- Neither selected raw compound nor recipe contains a CAS field. **Do not present the historical CAS or newly read supplier CAS as an original raw CAS assertion.**

## Bounded correction and acceptance

1. Prevent this source-supported P3556 material observation from collapsing onto `CHEBI:86658`; retain a source/material-scoped identity unless a separately reviewed suitably scoped target is established. Preserve source label, supplier attribute, full source record, assertion ID, quantities, units, and edge provenance/tier.
2. Retain the original mapping claim and supplier/native evidence in the appropriate review/audit trail. Review the generic MIM lexical/identity route upstream before rebuilding its derived aliases; do not erase the valid native molecular term or globally quarantine CAS `8002-43-5`.
3. Add a hermetic regression using this exact raw record and pinned native structure. Exercise the relevant unified route and prove a fallback cannot restore the same unsupported exact assignment; preserve an explicitly structure-qualified valid molecular use as a control. Removing the `86658` alias alone is insufficient: a possible alternative name/CAS route to `CHEBI:16110` (a generic charged class), or another unreviewed phosphatidylcholine target, is not automatically an approved identity for this supplied material. The trace did not claim to have executed every counterfactual fallback.
4. Rebuild/review the affected source candidate and compare the finite row delta. The measured current source cohort is **one recipe assertion**, not an asserted universal bound on future or other-source uses.

This issue does not demand remapping the two multivalued CAS-to-ChEBI xrefs, repairing CAS digits, dropping the recipe, editing the immutable supported MIM artifact, or asserting a new chemical equivalence based only on the product name. Current Activated carbon and KJ uses were independently traced and do not exhibit the suspected historical CAS-routing failure.

# Isolated replay helper admits output bytes after validating an earlier version

`data/issue1224-quarantine-20260929.xjuS9H/issue1236-review/run_mediadive_replay.py`

of that issue's undocumented historical234-ID cohort.

Current master:709652d7ae6985cd9c5d6bb40db6f01bc2ede351.
Actual reviewed archive SHA256:
`3e103a608852300a16cecbbb9e9b866ce1e156e96a68102bb14f9e0c2125c425`.
Complete staged-node enumeration finds eight standalone CAS-prefixed node IDs.
Seven pass syntax/checksum; one does not:

```text
id: cas:977046-75-5
name: Yeast autolysate
category: biolink:ChemicalEntity
provided_by: infores:mediadive
```

For the eight digits preceding its check digit, the weighted sum is
`5*1 + 7*2 + 6*3 + 4*4 + 0*5 + 7*6 + 7*7 + 9*8 = 216`.
`216 % 10 = 6`, which differs from the supplied5. The existing repository
`ingredient_bundle_contract.valid_cas` specifies this syntax/checksum contract;
CAS documents the check-digit requirement at
https://www.cas.org/es-es/training/documentation/chemical-substances/checkdig .
**Changing the last digit to6 is not an evidence-backed identity correction.**
Checksum validity alone would not establish the right substance either.

## Traceable inputs

- Unifiedfe54cd1a… line591139: `kgm.name:yeast_autolysate`, label
  `Yeast autolysate`, `skos:closeMatch`, object `cas:977046-75-5`, source
  `mediadive_compounds`. This is a historical consolidated route, not evidence
  that the pinned MIM supported export made this claim.
- `data/raw/compound_mappings_strict.tsv` and
  `data/raw/compound_mappings_strict_hydrate.tsv` lines9228/12771 retain the
  same value as `CAS-RN:977046-75-5` for DSMZ843/JCM18 yeast-autolysate rows.
- `data/raw/mediadive/compounds.json` record1603 contains
  `compound: Yeast autolysate`,5g,4.9505g_l; it has no embedded CAS value.
- MediaDive `standardize_compound_id` tries unified, legacy and embedded
  routes before its source-local ingredient fallback. All routes require
  regression coverage; changing one mapping row is not sufficient protection.

## Required resolution

1. Prevent syntactically/checksum-invalid CAS values from becoming active
   resolved identifiers across unified and relevant fallback routes.
2. Preserve rejected raw mapping evidence and source ingredient identity,
   recipe occurrence fields/quantities/citations; use an appropriate existing
   source-local fallback when no supported identity exists. Do not delete the
   ingredient, guess a CAS number, or conflate it with yeast extract.
3. Inventory active CAS-valued mapping endpoints and source/merged incidence
   with predicates and evidence roles kept distinct. Do not treat an annotation
   as exact identity, or close #286 on a selected eight-node checksum test.
4. Add offline regression tests for unified, legacy and embedded bypasses,
   valid identifiers and preserved complete source occurrences. Review any
   necessary consolidated-artifact regeneration separately from raw data/pins.
5. Independently review the implementation, run all required local/hosted
   gates, and verify rebuilt affected outputs before claiming graph correction.

No production mapping, source output or archive has been modified. Prior
finite MIM acceptance and exact serializer-delta evidence remain recorded;
they are not an exhaustive validation of every legacy CAS identity. This new
finding must be resolved/dispositioned before an unrestricted release claim.
title: Invalid CAS checksum for yeast autolysate survives unified and MediaDive fallback mappings

Found in the review of #1594 (#1576).

Split out from #680, which added a guard but did not fix the underlying cache design.

## Problem

Two caches in the MediaDive transform are permanent and unversioned:

1. `kg_microbe/transform_utils/mediadive/mediadive.py:139` — `requests_cache.install_cache("mediadive_cache")` is called with **no `expire_after`**. `mediadive_cache.sqlite` on this machine is 33 MB and holds `rest/solution/*` responses created in 2025 that are still served verbatim today.
2. `mediadive.py:759-762` — `get_json_object()` falls back to the per-medium YAML cache under `tmp/medium_yaml/`, guarded only by `if not fn.is_file():`. Freshness is never checked. Files there are dated **Oct 30 2023**.

## Impact (observed, not hypothetical)

`data/transformed/mediadive/edges.tsv` (Jul 24 15:38) was produced before `data/raw/mediadive/*.json` finished downloading (Jul 25 00:14), so the bulk path was unavailable and both caches took over. Result:

- `tmp/medium_yaml/916.yaml` (2023) records `solution_id: 1885` named `Solution F`.
- Current MediaDive has restructured this: `1885` is "Ferrous chloride solution (5.2%)", wrapped by a new solution `6570` named "Solution F".
- So the shipped output asserts `solution:1878 -has_part-> 1885`, skipping the wrapper, and emits a node `mediadive.solution:1885` labelled "Solution F". `mediadive.solution:6570` has no node row and no edges at all.

Drift scale: 22 KG solution subjects and 24 KG solution objects reference IDs absent from today's `solutions.json`; 13 raw solutions never appear as a KG subject.

## Suggested fix

- Give `requests_cache` an explicit `expire_after`, or key the cache on the MediaDive release/download date.
- Add invalidation (or at minimum an age check + warning) to the YAML medium cache.
- Consider dropping the YAML cache entirely now that bulk download is the supported path.

#680 makes the silent-fallback path refuse to run, which prevents recurrence of the *silent* failure, but the caches themselves are still unbounded and will serve stale data whenever they are used deliberately.
title: mediadive: YAML medium cache and requests_cache have no expiry or invalidation

MediaDive and BactoTraits both read the BacDive-generated `tmp/bacdive.tsv`, but their `TRANSFORM_INPUTS` declarations omit BacDive. body:
Found during the 2026-09-10 full rebuild, while working out why `mediadive` and `metatraits` were being run against a half-updated `data/transformed/ontologies/`.

## The gap

`Transform.TRANSFORM_INPUTS`' docstring says **five** cross-transform dependencies exist (gold, lpsn, lpsn_api, microbedecoder, prego). There are at least **eight**:

| transform | reads | declares |
|---|---|---|
| `bacdive` | `ontologies/ncbitaxon_nodes.tsv`, `ontologies/chebi_nodes.tsv` | `()` |
| `mediadive` | `ontologies/chebi_nodes.tsv` (ChEBI roles + categories) | `()` |
| `metatraits` | `ontologies/ncbitaxon_nodes.tsv` (`_load_ncbitaxon_labels`) | `()` |

`metatraits_gtdb` inherits metatraits' declaration, so it is affected too.

## Why the guard misses them

`tests/test_cross_transform_inputs.py` derives the real map by regexing three path idioms

```
transformed/<name>/ | output_base_dir / "<name>" | output_dir.parent / "<name>"
```

but only over `kg_microbe/transform_utils/<source>/**/*.py`. These three transforms never write such a path: they use constants defined in `constants.py`, which is outside the scanned tree.

```
CHEBI_NODES_FILE     = ONTOLOGIES_TRANSFORMED_DIR / "chebi_nodes.tsv"   → bacdive, mediadive
NCBITAXON_NODES_FILE = ONTOLOGIES_TRANSFORMED_DIR / "ncbitaxon_nodes.tsv" → bacdive, metatraits
```

`poetry run pytest tests/test_cross_transform_inputs.py` → **5 passed**. The test's own docstring says "Three prior versions of this same contract were opt-in and each was forgotten… This one is caught by the suite." It is not: expressing the dependency through a shared constant makes it invisible.

## Why it matters now

Two ways, both live:

1. **Freshness lies.** Re-running `ontologies` leaves bacdive, mediadive and metatraits genuinely stale while all three report `FRESH` — the #812 shape that #845 was meant to close.
2. **#685's skip logic cannot protect them.** When `ontologies` failed in this rebuild, `gold` and `prego` were correctly skipped because they declare it; `bacdive`, `mediadive` and `metatraits` ran anyway, against a directory holding five ontologies from the current run and eight from 2026-09-04. That is mixed-provenance output that looks clean.

## Fix

Resolve the constants when scanning: follow `*_NODES_FILE`-style names to their definition in `constants.py` and match `ONTOLOGIES_TRANSFORMED_DIR`-rooted paths, or invert the scan to start from the constants and find their users. Then declare the three dependencies.

Acceptance: the guard fails on today's code before the declarations are added, and `kgm-freshness-check` reports bacdive/mediadive/metatraits `STALE_VS_UPSTREAM` after an `ontologies` re-run.

Related: #812, #839, #845, #876 — the same contract, forgotten a fourth time.
title: Three transforms read ontologies output through a shared constant, so the cross-transform guard never sees the dependency
